title: BalancerPoolerV2 hook receives pre-wrap USDS amount, not the sUSDS shares actually held after _dispatch
rejectionNote: Severity-auditor: IDispatchHook NatSpec is already explicit that hooks receive the dispatch input amount. 'Future hook author might misread the spec' is not a finding.
description: BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch receives `amount` (the FOT-adjusted USDS that arrived on the dispatcher) and calls `IERC4626(_sUSDS).deposit(amount, address(this))`. After _dispatch returns, ATokenDispatcherV2.dispatch invokes `hook.onDispatch(minter, amount, extraData)` with the SAME `amount` value. Post-wrap, what the dispatcher actually holds is sUSDS shares, not USDS. IDispatchHook's doc (src/V2/interfaces/IDispatchHook.sol L6-L9) only states that the hook is called with the same tuple forwarded to dispatch. For hooks that track 'how much productive asset was received by this dispatcher', USDS amount is the wrong number because sUSDS.deposit may (in degenerate cases or with FOT-ish/pessimistic share price) issue a different number of shares, and the hook has no way to retrieve the share count without re-reading state. For other V2 dispatchers (BurnerV2, GatherV2) the unit of `amount` matches what the dispatcher acted on (tokens burned/forwarded), so BalancerPoolerV2 is the outlier.
impact: Semantic ambiguity in the hook interface. A hook that assumes `amount` represents the dispatcher's post-dispatch productive-asset delta will be wrong for BalancerPoolerV2. This does not lose funds today (DefaultDispatchHook is a no-op) but is a foot-gun for any future accounting/logging hook. Because V2 is explicitly designed so owner can swap hooks without code changes, this is the kind of silent contract-semantics gap that future integrations will trip over.
recommendation: Either (a) in BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch, capture IERC20(_sUSDS).balanceOf(address(this)) before and after the deposit, and override dispatch behavior to pass the share delta to the hook; or (b) extend IDispatchHook / introduce an overload (e.g. onDispatchV2(minter, inputAmount, outputAmount, outputAsset, extraData)); or (c) document in IDispatchHook that `amount` is the INPUT amount to _dispatch and may not equal the dispatcher's post-state asset position, and leave hook authors responsible for re-querying balances.
dedupNote: Unique. Concerns the hook callback semantics introduced by stories 025/026 (USDS->sUSDS wrap + onDispatch). Not present in round-01/02/03 findings (those round-03 BalancerPoolerV2 lows cover oracle/sandwich, not hook-amount semantics). Not covered by knownIssues.
sanitizeNote: In V2 focus area (stories 025+026: BalancerPoolerV2 USDS->sUSDS wrap + onDispatch hook semantics). Not owner-driven — the gap surfaces for any future hook integration regardless of who deploys it. No match against project knownIssues.
classifyNote: C4 regular-audit Low/QA. No present-day economic effect: the wrap to sUSDS executes correctly, share accounting on the dispatcher itself is correct, and DefaultDispatchHook is a no-op so the (semantically wrong) `amount` value is never consumed. No mis-accounting reaches NFT holders today. Mis-pricing surface only manifests if-and-when a future non-trivial hook is deployed that interprets `amount` as the post-wrap delta — i.e. future-code speculation, which C4 caps at QA. Spec/interface-clarity issue, not a value leak. Confirm Low.
validityNote: Borderline future-code speculation, but anchored in a present-day inconsistency: BalancerPoolerV2 is the outlier among V2 dispatchers (BurnerV2/GatherV2 pass amounts that match what the dispatcher acted on). That inconsistency is a real interface/spec gap today regardless of any future hook. Acceptable as QA / spec-clarity hardening item per C4 norms for Low findings.
